neighboring_unit_entries.title: Fractional-part functions give the original L2 closure and totality criterion
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The theorem realizes RH as approximation of the constant function and, equivalently, totality of a parameterized family of fractional-part functions in L2((0,1]).

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Fractional-part generators map to the analytic zeta family
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The calculation identifies the Mellin image of each f_lambda with minus F_lambda, making the two closure problems genuinely equivalent rather than merely analogous.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The Mellin representation preserves Hilbert distance while turning interval functions into analytic functions; interval indicators provide a total test family that extends norm preservation from simple differences to the whole L2 space.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines a Fourier-Mellin transform from L2((0,1]) into H^2(Omega), argues that each image is analytic, and uses indicator functions Psi_lambda together with a standard integral identity to establish equality of norms and pairwise distances. Since these indicators are total, the transform is an isometric embedding of the full source space.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a structure-preserving coordinate change: closure, totality, and approximation distances can be transported without distortion from a real-variable space to an analytic-function space.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The transform itself is the bridge, while the nested interval indicators are the dense scaffold on which isometry is checked and extended.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The passage establishes an isometric map into H^2(Omega), not a claim here that every Hardy function is in its range. Its displayed transform and auxiliary integral are too damaged to reconstruct safely from this text.
directed.uncertainty: High for exact formulas and limits because the extraction shows inconsistent or fragmented displays; lower for the stated analyticity, indicator totality, and isometric-embedding role.

supported: The span defines the Mellin-type map, states analyticity of each image, uses interval indicators and their pairwise distances, and concludes that the map is an isometric embedding of L2((0,1]) into H^2(Omega).
The candidate correctly warns that the span does not establish surjectivity and that the extracted transform and auxiliary integral cannot be reconstructed safely.
inference: Treating the indicator family as a dense scaffold on which norm preservation is established is a sound summary of the proof sketch.
unsupported_or_imported: The unqualified claim that 'totality' transports without distortion from the real-variable space to the analytic-function space overreaches the source: an isometric embedding transports density only to its closed range, not necessarily to all of H^2(Omega).
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Structure-preserving coordinate change' is acceptable for distances and source-space closure, but it obscures the crucial into-versus-onto distinction when paired with the totality claim.
context_or_ocr_risk: The transform display has a suspect upper limit and the auxiliary integral is fragmented; only the prose-supported isometric-embedding role is safe without the scan.
missed_mechanism: The conceptual reading should explicitly distinguish totality in L2, totality of the image family within the transform range, and totality in the whole Hardy space.
revision_instructions: Qualify the transport claim: the isometry preserves distances and closed-span relations in L2 and identifies them with the corresponding relations inside its closed image; do not claim totality in all of H^2(Omega) unless surjectivity is separately established.
